report.verdict: A revenue-only trading update that confirms the 2026 story: the estate shrink and a 1–2ppt bad-results hit took reported Q3 revenue down 7% to £406m (~$544m), while like-for-like constant-currency revenue fell 2% — a deceleration from +2% in H1 even with the July World Cup in the base. With no divisional, EBITDA or net-debt disclosure and no guidance during the offer period, the equity is now a bet on Bally's Intralot closing on time (headline 52p/~$0.70 all-share, shares ~42p/~$0.56) against a balance sheet already at 5.6x and drifting toward ~6x as the 40% RGD annualises.

summary: **Headline: reported revenue -7% to £406m (~$544m), -2% like-for-like constant currency.** The gap (~5ppt, c.£22m/~$29m on the £435.4m/~$583m Q3-25 base) is almost entirely the c.270 closed William Hill shops plus minor FX. The update is unaudited and carries no divisional revenue, EBITDA, cash or net-debt figures — management explicitly limited disclosure given the pending Bally's Intralot acquisition.

**Underlying deceleration, not stability.** LfL growth has gone +2% (Q1-26) → c.+2% (Q2-26, implied by H1 +2%) → -2% (Q3-26). Management attributes 1–2ppt of the Q3 decline to customer-friendly results at the start of the football season and calls revenue 'broadly stable on a normalised basis' — i.e. flat at best, versus +2% in H1, and that is with July's FIFA World Cup knockout rounds in the quarter. We read the normalised run-rate as roughly flat to slightly negative.

**Versus expectations: no formal consensus to beat or miss.** The Board withdrew medium-term targets on 26 Nov 2025 and has given no FY26 guidance since the 5 June 2026 offer. At H1 (12 Aug) they said post-period trading was 'in line with management expectations with strong levels of engagement throughout the FIFA World Cup'; Q3 is consistent with that only if 'in line' already assumed a sub-trend H2.

**Guidance bridge — there isn't one.** Old: FY25 adj. EBITDA margin ≥20% (delivered: 20.0%) and 5–9% p.a. revenue growth to 2027 (withdrawn). Interim: £125–135m (~$168–181m) annualised pre-mitigation duty headwind once fully implemented from Apr-27, ~£80m (~$107m) falling in FY26, with ~50% mitigation targeted. New: nothing quantified at Q3. The division that broke the old framework is UK&I Online (RGD 21%→40% from 1 Apr 2026), not Retail — Retail is the division being cut to pay for it.

**9M-26 revenue is £1,293.5m (~$1.73bn), -2.2% YoY** (9M-25: £1,323.2m/~$1.77bn). On our arithmetic FY26 revenue lands around £1.72–1.73bn (~$2.31–2.32bn), c.-3%, assuming Q4 reported -6% (Q4-25 base £458.7m/~$615m) [estimate].

**H1-26 remains the last hard profit print: adj. EBITDA £150.2m (~$201m), -9.5%, margin 16.9% (-180bps).** A £46m (~$62m) YoY duty step-up (gaming duties £233.4m/~$313m, 26.3% of revenue vs 21.1%) was more than half offset by marketing -18.5% to £115.8m (~$155m), 13.0% of revenue (16.0%), promo efficiency and opex savings. Reported EBITDA £124.8m (~$167m), -11.7%, after £25.4m (~$34m) net exceptionals; IFRS loss after tax £70.2m (~$94m); adj. PAT £1.9m (~$2.5m); IFRS EPS -15.6p (~-$0.21), adj. EPS 0.4p (~$0.005).

**UK&I Online is the profit engine despite being the duty epicentre:** H1 revenue +3.5% to £348.1m (~$467m), gaming +6.7% on William Hill Vegas, betting -2.4%, 888 managed down for margin; adj. EBITDA +28.3% to £77.0m (~$103m), margin 22.1% (+430bps) even with ~£30m (~$40m) of extra UK duty in Q2 alone. That mitigation leans heavily on marketing cuts, which is a finite lever.

**International has gone ex-growth:** H1 revenue -1.9% to £293.8m (~$394m) (Italy +21%, Denmark +13%; Spain, Romania, RoW down), actives -14% to 559k, adj. EBITDA -20.9% to £67.6m (~$91m), margin 23.0% (-560bps) on Italy/Romania duty rises and mix. Q1-26 International sports revenue was -29%. FY25's +9%/+35% growth engine is no longer carrying the group.

**Retail: smaller, more profitable, and now facing MGD 25%.** H1 reported revenue -2.6% to £245.6m (~$329m) but LfL +4%; adj. EBITDA +5.4% to £31.2m (~$42m), margin 12.7% (+100bps). The c.270 closures were stated to be loss-making shops. The 28 Oct 2026 Budget lifted Machine Games Duty from 20% to 25% on >£1-stake machines from 1 Apr 2027 — short of the 40% feared, but another £9–10m (~$12–13m) annualised gross cost on our estimate of the remaining machine base [estimate; Entain guided ~£25m for its larger estate].

**Event stats: none disclosed.** Unlike peers, evoke gave no World Cup revenue, stakes or actives data — only qualitative 'strong engagement' at H1. Group H1 KPIs: average monthly actives 1.631m (-6%), sportsbook stakes £2,099.7m (~$2.81bn) (-9%), net sports revenue margin 13.3% (+60bps, described as structural — pricing, mix, risk management), gaming revenue £608.3m (~$815m) (+2%), betting revenue £279.2m (~$374m) (-5%).

**Cost/mitigation programme:** target ~50% mitigation of the £125–135m (~$168–181m) annualised duty hit via supplier savings, reduced marketing, shop closures, opex cuts and proposition changes; H1 delivered >50% offset of the £46m (~$62m) gross headwind. Layered on top, Bally's Intralot has identified ~£180m (~$241m) of pre-tax cost and capex synergies by end of year two post-completion (marketing optimisation, operational efficiencies, IT infrastructure) — read: more UK marketing and overhead cuts.

**Capital position (30 Jun 26):** net debt £1,899.4m (~$2.55bn) (gross borrowings £1,919.8m/~$2.57bn, leases £85.2m/~$114m, cash ex-customer balances £105.6m/~$142m); RCF £157.0m (~$210m) drawn, £43.0m (~$58m) undrawn; total liquidity ~£150m (~$201m). Leverage 5.6x on LTM adj. EBITDA £340.4m (~$456m), up from 5.2x. Underlying FCF £85m (~$114m) in H1 after capex £50.9m (~$68m) and leases £22.3m (~$30m), but net interest paid £88.9m (~$119m) and £26.9m (~$36m) exceptional cash outflows pushed net debt up. No Q3 balance-sheet update was given; no dividend.

**Leverage direction is up.** LTM EBITDA will fall further as the 40% RGD annualises through Q3/Q4 (each quarter carries ~£25–30m/~$34–40m of incremental UK duty YoY before mitigation). We model FY26 adj. EBITDA of ~£300–320m (~$402–429m) and net debt roughly flat at ~£1.9bn (~$2.55bn), i.e. ~6x by YE26 [estimate]. Standalone, this is a refinancing story; the €889m second-lien facility (TPG, Oaktree, OHA) committed under the Intralot deal is what takes out the €450m 2028 FRNs and $575m 2028 TLB.

**Deal status: on track, with a new US regulatory wrinkle.** Both shareholder bases approved (evoke court meeting 99.91%, GM 99.63% on 17 Aug 2026); 'the majority' of regulatory approvals received; completion still guided to late Q4-26/early Q1-27. However, on 26 Oct Pennsylvania's Office of Enforcement Counsel objected to the joint petition for 888 Atlantic to conditionally surrender its interactive gaming manufacturer licence (legacy Caesars/WSOP B2B contract); a standard PGCB review could take 9+ months. The Board decides; conditions were proposed as a fallback.

**Terms recap:** 0.537 new Bally's Intralot shares per evoke share (52p/~$0.70 at €1.12), equity value £243.1m (~$326m), EV ~£2.2bn (~$2.95bn), cash alternative 52p capped at £117.1m (~$157m); evoke holders ~11.5% of the enlarged group. At 42.1p (~$0.56) the shares sit ~19% below headline terms — a function of Intralot's share price since June and residual completion risk; we could not verify Intralot's current price [unverified].

**Management is emphasising** 'resilience', 'profitability and cash generation' and the political case against further tax; **it is burying** the LfL deceleration, the absence of any profit or leverage data for the quarter, and the fact that Q2's 28% UK&I Online EBITDA growth was bought with an 18.5% marketing cut while actives fell 6% group-wide.

**Regulation remains the swing factor:** RGD 40% (live since 1 Apr 2026); remote GBD 15%→25% from 1 Apr 2027 (UK horse racing and SSBT bets exempt); MGD 20%→25% from 1 Apr 2027. The 2027 steps are not in any reported number yet. Shares rose ~3.5% to c.44.5p (~$0.60) on 28 Oct on relief that MGD was not doubled.

**Thesis read-through:** for evoke equity holders the operating print is now second-order; what matters is (i) PGCB/court timetable, (ii) Intralot's share price, and (iii) whether evoke's EBITDA erodes enough before closing to strain the combined group's covenants and the £180m synergy case. For the UK sector, Q3 corroborates that the online duty hike is being met with marketing withdrawal and estate rationalisation, which should favour scale leaders (Flutter, Entain, bet365) on share.

segments.name: UK & Ireland Online (William Hill, 888, Mr Green UK)
segments.headline: The duty epicentre is still the profit engine — but Q3 brought no numbers, and the mitigation is mostly marketing withdrawal.
narrative: They did not disclose UK&I Online revenue for Q3-26, so the divisional read has to be triangulated. The base is Q3-25 revenue of £163.3m (~$219m), +1% YoY, with sports £50.7m (~$68m) up 8% on weak prior-year margins and gaming roughly £112.6m (~$151m) down 2%. Through 2026 the division had been the one part of the group growing: Q1-26 revenue of £170m (~$228m) was +5% (gaming +8%, sports -2%) and H1-26 revenue of £348.1m (~$467m) was +3.5%, implying a Q2 of roughly £178m (~$239m). Against that, the group statement that 'particularly customer-friendly sports results in the beginning of the football season' cost 1–2ppt of group growth (c.£4–9m/~$5–12m) lands disproportionately here and in Retail, since International sports is only c.10% of that division's revenue. Our working assumption is that UK&I Online revenue was broadly flat to modestly up YoY in Q3, with gaming still growing and sports down [estimate, unverified].

The H1 economics remain the best evidence of how the division is being run. Average monthly actives were 1.072m, slightly down on FY25's 1.1m, and 888 revenue continued to fall by design as they prioritised 'profitability and customer economics rather than pursuing lower-return volume'; William Hill delivered double-digit gaming growth on William Hill Vegas product improvements and 'more effective bonusing', taking divisional gaming revenue +6.7% while betting fell 2.4%. Cost of sales rose to £151.7m (~$203m) from £124.2m (~$166m), of which roughly £30m (~$40m) was the 1 April 2026 step-up in Remote Gaming Duty from 21% to 40% — booked for only one quarter in H1. Despite that, adjusted EBITDA rose 28.3% to £77.0m (~$103m) and margin expanded 430bps to 22.1% from 17.8%. The arithmetic only works because group marketing was cut 18.5% to £115.8m (~$155m), or 13.0% of revenue from 16.0%, and because the group sportsbook net revenue margin improved 60bps to 13.3% on what they describe as structural pricing, mix and risk-management changes rather than results.

We are sceptical that this is repeatable at the same rate. Q3 and Q4 each carry a full quarter of the 19-point RGD increase against a 21% comparator, so the YoY duty drag in UK&I Online in H2 is roughly double H1's. Marketing can only be cut once; the FY25 statement already flagged black-market share gains in UK horse racing and 12% lower UK&I Online betting revenue in 2025, and group actives were down 6% in H1. From 1 April 2027 remote General Betting Duty rises from 15% to 25% (UK horse racing and in-shop SSBT bets exempt), which is the second leg of the £125–135m (~$168–181m) annualised pre-mitigation group headwind the company quantified in November 2025 and which is in no reported number yet. The company's own target is to mitigate about half.

No segment guidance was given and none should be expected before completion. Under Bally's Intralot the stated plan is to deploy Intralot technology to the evoke brands and to extract ~£180m (~$241m) of cost and capex synergies by the end of year two, led by 'marketing spend optimisation' — in a market where evoke has already reduced marketing intensity by three points of revenue. The UK online market-share consequence of that is the thing to watch in Gambling Commission data; we have no evoke-disclosed share figures for the division and will not estimate one.

segments.name: UK Retail (William Hill shops)
segments.headline: The -7% headline is the estate shrink; the remaining shops are more profitable, but MGD 25% from April 2027 is the next cost to absorb.
narrative: They did not disclose Retail revenue for Q3-26 either, but Retail is where the reported/LfL gap lives: reported -7% versus -2% like-for-like constant currency is c.5ppt, or roughly £22m (~$29m) on the £435.4m (~$583m) Q3-25 group base, nearly all of it the c.270 shops that are no longer trading (c.70 closed in Q4-25 and c.200 from 24 May 2026) with a small FX residual in International. The Q3-25 Retail base was £121.7m (~$163m), +6%, split betting £67.1m (~$90m) and gaming £54.6m (~$73m), both +6%, helped by soft prior-year win margins and the 5,000 new gaming cabinets rolled out by March 2025. Stripping c.£20m of closed-shop revenue from that base implies Q3-26 Retail revenue somewhere around £100m (~$134m), before any LfL movement and before the customer-friendly football results they cited [estimate, unverified].

The H1-26 print showed what the rationalisation is meant to achieve. Reported revenue fell 2.6% to £245.6m (~$329m), yet like-for-like revenue was +4% (Q1-26 LfL +3%, gaming +6%, sports flat), supported by the gaming-machine estate and 2,000 new self-service betting terminals. Adjusted EBITDA rose 5.4% to £31.2m (~$42m) and margin expanded 100bps to 12.7% as loss-making locations came out of the P&L. For context, FY25 Retail revenue was £501.0m (~$671m), -1%, and adjusted EBITDA £55.0m (~$74m), -17%, with the Board taking £440.3m (~$590m) of impairments across Retail and UK Online in FY25 on the new tax regime and 'challenging high street trading conditions'. The division's fixed cost base means the LfL growth and closures matter more to profit than the reported revenue line suggests.

The post-period development is the 28 October 2026 Budget, in which Machine Games Duty was lifted from 20% to 25% on machines with stakes above £1 from 1 April 2027 — well short of the 40% lobbied for by campaigners. Entain estimated c.£25m (~$34m) of annualised incremental retail cost for its roughly twice-as-large estate; scaling to evoke's remaining machine base (Q3-25 retail gaming revenue of £54.6m annualises to ~£218m/~$292m pre-closures, perhaps £175–195m/~$235–261m after) implies a gross hit in the order of £9–10m (~$12–13m) a year [our estimate]. Per Widerström said evoke is 'concerned about the impact of further taxation on the regulated UK betting industry' while welcoming that the rate was not raised to the levels floated. The market treated it as relief: evoke shares rose about 3.5% to c.44.5p (~$0.60) on the day.

Our judgement is that Retail is now a managed-decline cash asset whose job is to fund the online duty bill, and that further estate rationalisation under Bally's Intralot ownership is more likely than not once MGD lands in 2027 — Entain's own mitigation plan explicitly includes 'estate rationalisation'. The one structural positive is that in-shop SSBT bets stay at 15% General Betting Duty and are not treated as remote, which keeps the omni-channel pivot (Acca Boost, SSBT growth) tax-efficient relative to the 25% remote rate arriving in April 2027. No Retail guidance was given.

segments.name: International Online (Italy, Spain, Denmark, Romania, RoW)
segments.headline: FY25's growth engine is now ex-growth with a 560bps margin reset; Italy and Denmark are carrying a shrinking active base.
narrative: They did not break out International for Q3-26. The Q3-25 base was £150.4m (~$202m), +6% reported (+8% at constant currency per the company's Q3-25 summary), with double-digit growth in Italy, Denmark and Romania and Spain lagging; 9M-25 International revenue was £449.9m (~$603m), +11%. The 2026 trajectory has been negative: Q1-26 revenue of £148m (~$198m) was -2% with gaming +2% but sports -29%, and H1-26 revenue of £293.8m (~$394m) was -1.9%, implying a Q2 of roughly £146m (~$195m). Italy grew 21% and Denmark 13% in H1, offset by declines in Spain, Romania and Rest of World. Given FX is the only non-closure item in the LfL adjustment, the small gap between reported and constant-currency in Q3 suggests the division was not a large swing factor either way [inference].

The customer economics show a deliberate shrink. Average monthly actives fell 14% to 559k from 652k as they stepped away from lower-value acquisition, while gaming revenue held flat at £265.9m (~$356m); by subtraction sports revenue was only c.£28m (~$37m), down sharply, so International is effectively a casino business with a sportsbook attached. Cost of sales rose to £121.7m (~$163m) from £110.4m (~$148m), reflecting roughly £16m (~$21m) of additional duty in Italy and Romania, and an adverse mix shift toward higher-duty markets. Adjusted EBITDA fell 20.9% to £67.6m (~$91m) (the presentation shows £68.1m on a different allocation) and margin compressed 560bps to 23.0% from 28.6%; FY25's margin had been 28.9% on adjusted EBITDA of £175.4m (~$235m), +35%.

Operationally the platform consolidation continued — Mr Green has migrated to the in-house 888 platform across markets, Denmark moved in-house in 2025 and 888 Romania moved onto the Winner.ro platform after the Winner acquisition — and FY25 cash flow carried c.£16m (~$21m) of Italian licence and guarantee costs for the new concession regime. Those are the structural items; the cyclical one is sports margin, where International's Q1 -29% suggests both volume loss and unfavourable results. None of this was updated at Q3.

Our view is that International's value to the combined group is as a regulated, locally-licensed footprint (Bally's Intralot named the UK, Ireland, Spain, Denmark, Romania and Italy as its six core markets) rather than as a growth asset in 2026–27. With actives down 14% and margin down 560bps, the H2 comparison against FY25's record Italy/Denmark revenues is tough, and we would not model a return to growth before Intralot's technology and lottery adjacencies are in place. No segment guidance was given.

highlights.text: UK&I Online adj. EBITDA +28.3% to £77.0m (~$103m) in H1-26 with margin +430bps to 22.1%, delivered in the first quarter of 40% RGD — evidence the mitigation plan has real teeth.
More than half of the £46m (~$62m) gross H1 duty headwind was offset; group marketing cut 18.5% to 13.0% of revenue (from 16.0%) while UK&I Online revenue still grew 3.5%.
Sportsbook net revenue margin +60bps to 13.3% in H1, attributed to pricing, mix and risk management rather than results — a structural lever that partly cushions Q3's bad football results.
Retail rationalisation is working on its own terms: H1 LfL revenue +4%, adj. EBITDA +5.4% to £31.2m (~$42m), margin +100bps, with the c.270 closed shops described as loss-making.

Bally's Intralot acquisition 'remains on track': 99.9% shareholder approval, majority of regulatory approvals received, €889m second-lien (TPG/Oaktree/OHA) committed to refinance the €450m 2028 FRNs and $575m 2028 TLB — the standalone refinancing wall goes away on completion.
28 Oct Budget set MGD at 25% (from 20%) on >£1 machines, not the 40% feared; evoke shares +~3.5% to c.44.5p (~$0.60). Our gross estimate of the hit is ~£9–10m (~$12–13m) p.a. [estimate].
Net interest paid fell to £88.9m (~$119m) from £103.6m (~$139m) after the 2025 refinancing of the 2027 EUR notes (8.0% 2031s), and underlying FCF was £85m (~$114m) in H1.

lowlights.text: LfL cc revenue -2% in Q3 after +2% in Q1 and H1 — a 4ppt deceleration even with the July World Cup in the quarter; 'normalised broadly stable' is flat at best.

Reported revenue -7% to £406m (~$544m); 9M-26 -2.2% to £1,293.5m (~$1.73bn). On our arithmetic FY26 revenue is ~-3% and FY26 adj. EBITDA ~£300–320m (~$402–429m) vs £356.2m (~$477m) in FY25 [estimate].

Leverage 5.6x at June and rising mechanically as LTM EBITDA absorbs two more quarters of 40% RGD; we see ~6x by YE26 on ~£1.9bn (~$2.55bn) net debt [estimate]. Liquidity was ~£150m (~$201m) with £157m (~$210m) of the RCF drawn.
International: actives -14% to 559k, adj. EBITDA -20.9% to £67.6m (~$91m), margin -560bps to 23.0%; Q1 sports revenue -29%. The FY25 growth engine is now a drag.

Information vacuum: no divisional revenue, EBITDA, cash or net debt in the Q3 update and no guidance — the fourth consecutive quarter without a quantified outlook since targets were withdrawn on 26 Nov 2025.

Pennsylvania's Office of Enforcement Counsel (26 Oct) objected to the 888 Atlantic licence-surrender petition tied to the Caesars/WSOP B2B contract; a standard PGCB review could take 9+ months and threatens the late-Q4-26/early-Q1-27 completion window.

Two more duty steps are unbooked: remote GBD 15%→25% from 1 Apr 2027 (part of the £125–135m/~$168–181m annualised pre-mitigation estimate) and MGD 20%→25% from 1 Apr 2027. Corporate costs also jumped to £25.6m (~$34m) from £9.2m (~$12m) in H1 within adjusted EBITDA.

Shares at ~42p (~$0.56) sit ~19% below the 52p (~$0.70) headline all-share terms — the consideration floats with Intralot's share price and carries completion risk; group actives fell 6% in H1 while marketing was cut, so the underlying franchise is shrinking into the deal.

forecast.intro: There is no company guidance to bridge. The pre-November-2025 framework (revenue +5–9% p.a. to 2027; FY25 adj. EBITDA margin ≥20%) was withdrawn after the UK Budget raised Remote Gaming Duty to 40% from 1 Apr 2026 and introduced a 25% remote betting rate from 1 Apr 2027. The company's only quantification since is a £125–135m (~$168–181m) annualised pre-mitigation duty headwind once fully implemented, ~£80m (~$107m) of it in FY26, with ~50% mitigation targeted; H1-26 offset over half of a £46m (~$62m) gross hit. At H1 and again at Q3 the Board declined to give forward-looking guidance because of the recommended Bally's Intralot acquisition. The division that drove the regime change is UK&I Online (duty), while Retail is where the revenue line is shrinking (closures) and International is where margin has reset (Italy/Romania duty, mix).

forecast.view: **Q4-26:** we expect reported revenue of roughly £430m (~$576m), c.-6% YoY against a £458.7m (~$615m) Q4-25 base, with the closed estate still worth ~5ppt and LfL around -1% to flat; a normal football margin would recover 1–2ppt of Q3's results drag. **FY26:** revenue ~£1,725m (~$2.31bn), -3%. On EBITDA, H2-25 adjusted EBITDA was £190.3m (~$255m); H2-26 absorbs ~£55–65m (~$74–87m) of gross incremental duty (two full quarters of UK RGD at ~£25–30m each plus Italy/Romania), which at >50% mitigation plus the retail closure benefit nets to a ~£25–35m (~$34–47m) hit, so H2-26E adj. EBITDA of ~£150–170m (~$201–228m) and **FY26E ~£300–320m (~$402–429m), margin ~18%** — down from 20.0%. **Leverage** drifts up mechanically: with H2 cash interest of ~£90m (~$121m), capex ~£40m (~$54m), leases ~£20m (~$27m) and deal/exceptional costs, net debt ends the year around £1.9bn (~$2.55bn) and **leverage ~6x** [all estimates]. **Swing factors:** football margins in Q4; the pace of 888 attrition versus William Hill gaming growth; Italy/Denmark momentum; any further acceleration of shop closures ahead of MGD; and, dominating everything, whether the PGCB accepts the 888 Atlantic workaround so the scheme can be sanctioned in the guided window. If completion slips into mid-2027, evoke faces the April 2027 GBD and MGD steps as a standalone 6x-levered credit with ~£150m (~$201m) of liquidity — the scenario the Board's strategic review was designed to avoid.
watch: PGCB ruling on the 888 Atlantic licence-surrender petition (OEC objected 26 Oct 2026) and any change to the late-Q4-26/early-Q1-27 completion guidance; court sanction date.
Bally's Intralot share price versus the €1.12 reference — the all-share consideration (0.537 new shares) floats; the cash alternative (52p, capped at £117.1m/~$157m) is the only fixed element.
FY25-style post-close trading update (likely January 2027): Q4 revenue by division, FY26 adj. EBITDA versus our £300–320m (~$402–429m), year-end net debt and leverage.
UK Gambling Commission market data for William Hill/888 online share as marketing is cut further; 888 brand attrition versus William Hill Vegas growth.
Implementation detail of remote GBD 25% and MGD 25% from 1 April 2027 and any further evoke estate rationalisation announcement.
Covenant headroom and liquidity: RCF drawn £157m (~$210m) / undrawn £43m (~$58m) at June; cash ex-customer balances £105.6m (~$142m).
Integration signals from Bally's Intralot on the £180m (~$241m) synergy phasing and Intralot platform deployment to evoke brands.

report.sharePriceReaction: Broadly flat on the day: shares traded -0.5% at 41.90p (~$0.56) after the 7:00am release and closed at c.42.1p (~$0.56), unchanged versus the 22 Oct close, with the stock pinned to the Bally's Intralot all-share terms (headline 52p/~$0.70; market cap ~£189m/~$253m). On 28 Oct the shares rose ~3.5% to c.44.5p (~$0.60) after the Budget set MGD at 25% rather than the 40% some had feared.
